A NHTSA infographic floated across my screen lately. I can't be the only one who noticed that the list of states with the most car thefts is a pretty solid reflection of population, and perhaps population density, suggesting people are pretty much people everywhere. But what is up with Missouri punching way above its weight? And Georgia isn't even in the top 10 - Good job! If you look instead at THEFT RATE PER RESIDENT, the picture changes some...DC off the charts in car thefts, but has such a small population that it doesn't show up in NHTSA's graphic. Statistically, we expect outliers to be small groups like that. California, though, is next in line for rate. After DC, the next four are geographic neighbors. Hmmm. Something in the water? Be careful of how you interpret statistical data, eh?
Peace. -W

As part of our ongoing efforts to promote transparency and enhance crime prevention awareness, Hawaiʻi Police Department is offering crime mapping data of Hawaiʻi Island. A free service by City Protect.com, this mobile-friendly website allows users to explore crime mapping of their neighborhood and district.

## How to Use
To see crimes in your neighborhood, zoom in on the map by clicking on the “+” sign in the lower right screen showing the outline of Hawaiʻi Island.
Once you’ve zoomed in on an area, click on “Incident” on the top left side of the page. Then click “filters”, type in a specific time frame and the types of crimes you would like to see, then hit enter. You can click on each icon on the map to read more information on that crime.

## How to Use
### Disclaimer
The CityProtect.com map represents statistics by geographic area for crimes reported to the Hawaiʻi Police Department Dispatch system. Data represented is a snapshot of the number of categorized incidents as recorded at the moment of data upload by CityProtect.com. The information may not always reflect changes to individual incidents/cases if the changes were made after data upload. Because the original data source is dynamic and is therefore constantly changing, information may differ from day to day. Crimes are subject to change for a variety of reasons, including late reporting, and reclassification of some offenses.
By posting this information the Hawaiʻi Police Department does not intend to make any inference, judgment, or representation as to the relative safety of any particular area or neighborhood.

## State of Hawaii Department of the Attorney General's Post
Under the nationally standardized definitions and reporting rules of NIBRS, a total of 54,089 “Group A” criminal offenses were reported across Hawaiʻi during calendar year 2025, yielding a rate of 3,775.0 offenses per 100,000 resident population and marking an 11.6% decrease in the state’s total crime rate since 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-5.7%) and property (-16.1%), while the rate of crimes against society (e.g., drug and “vice” offenses, weapon law violations) rose 0.9%. A total of 24.5% (13,260) of the reported offenses were cleared by arrest or exceptional means (e.g., death of the offender, offender already in custody in another jurisdiction), marking an increase from the 22.7% clearance rate reported for 2024.
As compared to the tallies in 2024, notable decreases were reported for the following offenses statewide in 2025: murder (-24.2%), negligent manslaughter (-22.2%), forcible sex offenses (-23.4%), robbery (-13.9%), assault (-5.3%), kidnapping (-6.8%), motor vehicle theft (-21.9%), arson (-31.4%), larceny/theft (-19.8%), fraud (-14.7%), counterfeiting/forgery (-19.9%), prostitution (-5.0%) and weapon law violations (-3.5%). Increases were reported for burglary (7.2%), drug offenses (0.2%) and gambling offenses (10.0%). The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard presents data for 51 specific offense types.

## State of Hawaii Department of the Attorney General's Post
Under the nationally standardized definitions and reporting rules of NIBRS, a total of 54,089 “Group A” criminal offenses were reported across Hawaiʻi during calendar year 2025, yielding a rate of 3,775.0 offenses per 100,000 resident population and marking an 11.6% decrease in the state’s total crime rate since 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-5.7%) and property (-16.1%), while the rate of crimes against society (e.g., drug and “vice” offenses, weapon law violations) rose 0.9%. A total of 24.5% (13,260) of the reported offenses were cleared by arrest or exceptional means (e.g., death of the offender, offender already in custody in another jurisdiction), marking an increase from the 22.7% clearance rate reported for 2024.
As compared to the tallies in 2024, notable decreases were reported for the following offenses statewide in 2025: murder (-24.2%), negligent manslaughter (-22.2%), forcible sex offenses (-23.4%), robbery (-13.9%), assault (-5.3%), kidnapping (-6.8%), motor vehicle theft (-21.9%), arson (-31.4%), larceny/theft (-19.8%), fraud (-14.7%), counterfeiting/forgery (-19.9%), prostitution (-5.0%) and weapon law violations (-3.5%). Increases were reported for burglary (7.2%), drug offenses (0.2%) and gambling offenses (10.0%). The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard presents data for 51 specific offense types.
